question: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency’s Safety Information Bulletin 2021-061 and subsequent guidance advised aircrew to temporarily refrain from operating following COVID-19 vaccination to mitigate the risk of side effects impairing safe performance. Under Regulation (EU) No 1178/20112 (Part-Medical provisions), licence holders are obliged to self-ground in the event of any decrease in medical fitness.
Comprehensive and comparable EU-wide data is essential in order to assess both the scale of such side effects and the potential safety consequences. 1.

Since the start of COVID-19 vaccination in the EU, how many occurrences of in-flight or pre-flight pilot incapacitation, grounding by an operator, or refusal of medical clearance have been recorded in temporal proximity to vaccination?

Of the pilots who self-grounded because of post-vaccination side effects, how many sought and obtained clearance from an aero-medical examiner or other authorised practitioner before resuming flight duties?

What is the Commission’s assessment of the safety risks to EU civil aviation arising from post-vaccination side effects in pilots, and what measures does it consider necessary to mitigate such risks in the future?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.10.2025) Incapacitation or poor performance of the flight crew due to medical reasons is one of the safety risks monitored by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) who conducts aviation safety risk assessments and assists and advises the European Commission on aviation safety matters.

After COVID vaccination started in the EU, EASA was not able to confirm any inflight incapacitation related to vaccination, nor any severe adverse reaction to vaccination affecting flight safety. This conclusion was reached after contacts with medical assessors of the National Aviation Authorities, and a review of occurrence reports and safety investigation reports to which the Agency has access.
Since EASA has to date not detected any serious adverse reactions to vaccination that affect aviation safety, no mitigation measures are required.
